Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:11:1.hebrew: מלאתך ודמעך וגו' - וסמיך ליה: "וכן תעשה לשורך לצאנך וגו'". ודרשינן הכי: "בכור בניך תתן לי" — "וכן לצאנך", דכי היכי דבכור בניך מצותו לאחר שלשים, כדכתיב (במדבר י״ח:ט״ו-ט״ז): "ופדויו מבן חדש תפדה" — אף בכור צאן לאחר שלשים. "מלאתך ודמעך", דהיינו בכורים — "כן לשורך", דכי היכי דבכורים לאחר חמשים, שהרי בפסח התבואה מתבשלת, ואין מביאין בכורים עד שיביאו שתי הלחם בעצרת, כדאמרינן בפרק רבי ישמעאל (מנחות סח:):
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:11:1.english: The fullness of your harvest, and the outflow of your presses, etc. - And adjacent to it is: “So you shall do with your oxen, with your sheep, etc.” (Exodus 22:29). And we expound as follows: “You shall give to Me your firstborn sons” [is juxtaposed with] “and so for your sheep” — for just as with a firstborn son, his mitzvah is after thirty [days], as it is written: “And their redemption from a month old you shall redeem” (Numbers 18:16) — so too, a firstborn of the flock [is given] after thirty [days]. “The fullness of your harvest and the outflow of your presses” — which is first fruits — [is juxtaposed with] “so for your oxen”, for just as first fruits [are brought] after fifty [days] — since at Passover the grain ripens, yet they do not bring first fruits until they bring the Two Loaves on Shavuot, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Yishmael (Menachot 68b) — [so too, a firstborn ox is given after fifty days].

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:12:1.hebrew: דמקדם לדמקדם - מלאתך ודמעך קודמין בפסוק ראשון, הלכך דרשינן להו אשורך הקודם בפסוק שני:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:12:1.english: That which is earlier [corresponds] to that which is earlier - “The fullness of your harvest and the outflow of your presses” come earlier in the first verse; therefore, we expound them [as applying] to “your ox,” which comes earlier in the second verse.

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:12:2.hebrew: ודמאחר - בכור בניך, דמאחר בפסוק ראשון, דרשינן ליה אצאנך המאוחר בפסוק שני:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:12:2.english: And that which is later - “The firstborn of your sons,” which is later in the first verse, we expound regarding “your sheep,” which is later in the second verse.

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:12:3.english: [That which is] adjacent to it to [that which is] adjacent - And “the firstborn of your sons” is adjacent to “your ox”.

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:14:1.english: And say sixty [days] - For we require that the other "doing" [be] similar to that of "the firstborn of your sons."

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:14:2.hebrew: לא מסרך הכתוב אלא לחכמים - הואיל ולא גילה לך שיעור עשייה שתוסיף, ודאי לחכמים מסרך, שיפרשו לך הטעם, ואחריהם תלך:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:14:2.english: The verse entrusted you only to the Sages - Since it did not reveal to you the measure of the [additional] “doing” that you are to add, it certainly entrusted you to the Sages, so that they would explain the rationale to you, and you shall follow after them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:16:1.english: Its tending - The trouble [involved with it].

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:16:2.hebrew: ששיניה דקות - ואינה יכולה לאכול עשב, ואם לא תהא עם האם, תמות:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:16:2.english: Because its teeth are small - And it is unable to eat grass, and if it is not with [its] mother, it will die.

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:17:1.hebrew: שנראה ככהן המסייע בבית הגרנות - לפי שבזמן הזה אין בכור ראוי לכלום עד שיפול בו מום, וכיון דעל ישראל רמיא ליטפל בו חמשים יום, ואמר ליה הכהן בתוך הזמן "תנהו לי ואזוננו, ואף על פי שלא אהנה" — דומה כמי ששוכרו ומצילו מן הטורח, ובלבד שיתננו לו ולא לכהן אחר; ודומה לכהן שמסייע בבית הגרנות לדוש ולזרות כדי שיתנו לו התרומות. אבל אם היה בעל מום, ואמר "תן לי שאוכלנו" — הואיל וחזי ליה, לא הוי ככהן המסייע:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:17:1.english: Because he appears like a priest who assists at the threshing floor - Since in the present era, a firstborn is not fit for anything until a blemish befalls it, and since it is incumbent upon an Israelite to tend to it for fifty days, and the priest said to him within that period: "Give it to me and I will feed it, even though I will derive no benefit [from it yet]" — he is considered like one who hires him and saves him from the burden, provided that he gives it to him and not to another priest; and he is similar to a priest who assists at the threshing floor to thresh and winnow so that they will give him the teruma. However, if it was blemished and [the priest] said: "Give [it] to me so that I may eat it" — since it is fit for him, he is not like an assisting priest.

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:18:1.hebrew: בבית הרועים - אכהנים קאי, כדי ליתן להם הבכורות:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:18:1.english: In the house of the shepherds - [This] refers to the priests, so that [the owners] will give them the firstborn [animals].

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:18:2.hebrew: בבית הגרנות - אכולהו קאי: כהנים מפני תרומות, ולוים משום מעשר ראשון, ועניים משום מעשר עני:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:18:2.english: At the threshing floors - It refers to all of them: Priests, because of terumot; and Levites, because of the first tithe; and the poor, because of the poor man's tithe.

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:18:3.hebrew: בבית המטבחים - אכהנים קאי, משום זרוע, לחיים וקיבה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:18:3.english: In the slaughterhouse - [This] refers to the priests, on account of the foreleg, the cheeks, and the abomasum.

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:1:1.english: That primarily it does not come for atonement - For one does not bring it for a sin.

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:1:2.hebrew: כיון דמכפרא אעשה - דעולה מכפרת על עשה, כדאמרינן במס' יומא (דף לו.): על עולה מתוודה עון שכחה ופאה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:1:2.english: Since it effects atonement for a positive [commandment] - For a burnt offering effects atonement for [neglecting] a positive [commandment], as we say in Tractate Yoma (daf 36a): Over a burnt offering, one confesses the iniquity of [omitting] forgotten sheaves and the corner [of the field].

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:20:2.hebrew: מן הפטור על החיוב - דשמא יהו להם שני סאין: אחד של טבל גמור, ואחד הופרש ממנה לכהן המסייע. ואי אמרת ליה דהדרא ולפרוש מינה משום קנסא, סבר בעל הבית: טבל גמור הוא, ומפריש ממנה עלה דאידך; ואיהי פטורה מדאורייתא, אלא קנסא הוא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:20:2.english: From the exempt for the obligated - Lest they have two se’ahs: one of completely untithed produce [tevel gamur], and one from which [teruma] was separated for the priest who assisted [them]. And if you say to him that it reverts [to being untithed] and he should separate from it due to the penalty, the homeowner will think: It is completely untithed produce, and he will separate from it on behalf of the other [se’ah]; whereas it is exempt by Torah law, and [its untithed status] is merely a penalty.

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:4:1.hebrew: והאנן נשר תנן - אלמא בנשר שרי עקביא, ולא בתלושין:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:4:1.english: But didn’t we learn: Was shed? - Evidently, Akavya permits [it only] when it was shed, but not when plucked.

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:5:1.hebrew: עיקרו הפוך כלפי ראשו - שכפול באמצעיתו, ושני ראשין נראין בחוץ:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:5:1.english: Its root is overturned toward its top - That it is folded in its middle, and both ends are visible on the outside.

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:5:2.hebrew: שאינו מתמעך - שאינו שוה עם הגיזה, אלא נראה עולה למעלה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:5:2.english: That is not compressed - That it is not level with the fleece, but rather appears rising upward:

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:6:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא לא אמר כרב נתן - הא ודאי, כיון דאינו מתמעך, "אינו נראה עם הגיזה" קרינא ביה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:6:1.english: What is the reason [Reish Lakish] did not state [his opinion] in accordance with Rav Natan - For surely, since it is not compressed, we read regarding it: "It does not appear with the fleece."

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:6:2.hebrew: לפי שאי אפשר לשום גיזה בלא נימין המדולדלות - שעולות למעלה, ואי כי האי גוונא מיתסר — אין לך גיזה מותרת. רבי נתן טפי מחמיר, להכי לא בעי: מאי טעמא לא אמר כריש לקיש:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:6:2.english: Because it is impossible for any fleece [to be] without dangling threads - Which rise upward; and if [wool] of this sort were prohibited, you would have no fleece [that is] permitted. Rabbi Natan is more stringent; therefore, [the Gemara] did not ask: What is the reason [he] did not state [his view] in accordance with Reish Lakish?

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:8:1.hebrew: עד כמה: ליטפל בבכור - בזמן הזה, קודם שיתננו לכהן, שמוזהר לעכבו אצלו בעל כרחו ולפרנסו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:8:1.english: Until when: To tend to the firstborn - During this period, before he gives it to the priest, in that he is instructed to keep it with him against his will and sustain it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:8:2.english: He may not give [it] to him - [The reason is] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:8:3.hebrew: אם היה בעל מום ואומר לו - הכהן בתוך הזמן: "תנהו לי שאוכלנו" — מותר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:8:3.english: If it was blemished and [the priest] says to him - The priest [says to him] within that period: "Give it to me so that I may eat it" — [it is] permitted [to give it to him].

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:9:1.english: Whether unblemished - In the time when the Temple is standing.

Rashi on Bekhorot 26b:9:2.english: Whether blemished - In the present time.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 26b:11:1.hebrew: מלאתך ודמעך לא תאחר כן תעשה לשורך - דהיינו נ' ימים, מיום הבאת העומר בפסח — שגמר זמן בישול התבואה — עד העצרת, שמביאין שתי הלחם להתיר חדש במקדש. וא"ת: האי ביום חמשים הוא, ולא הוי כעין "בכור בניך וצאנך תתן לי", דלאחר שלשים:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 26b:11:1.english: “You shall not delay the fullness of your harvest and of your outflow; so you shall do with your ox” - That is fifty days, from the day of the bringing of the Omer on Passover — for the completion of the grain’s ripening time is until Atzeret — when they bring the Two Loaves to permit the new [grain] in the Temple. And if you say: But this is on the fiftieth day, and [thus] is not like “the firstborn of your sons [and] your flock you shall give to Me,” which is after thirty [days]?

Tosafot on Bekhorot 26b:19:1.hebrew: וכי תימא מיתה לא תלמוד לומר וכו' - לאו דוקא, דלא חשיב לה בפרק אלו הן הנשרפין (סנהדרין פג.) בהדי אלו שבמיתה; אלא קרוב הוא [לעון] מיתה:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 26b:19:1.english: "And if you would say [that one is] not [punished by] death, the verse states, etc." - [This is] not literal, as [the Mishnah] does not count this in the chapter [entitled] Elu Hen HaNisrafin (Sanhedrin 83a) among those who are [liable to] death; rather, it is close to [the iniquity of] death.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 26b:20:1.hebrew: דלמא אתי לאפרושי מן הפטור על החיוב כו' - בכמה מקומות אמרינן: תרומה ויחזור ויתרום, ולא גזרינן. התם, כיון שהתרומה ראשונה לכהן, מידע ידע דשניה דרבנן; ואפילו נתן הראשונה כבר לכהן קודם שיאמר לו חכם לחזור ולתרום, מ"מ מדאין הכהן מחזיר לו את הראשונה, מידע ידע דשניה דרבנן היא. אבל כאן, סבור הוא שנתן לכהן בתורת שכר סיועו, ומעכבה כהן. ובכמה מקומות צריך לחלק בדברים: כי ההיא דפסחים בריש מקום שנהגו (פסחים דף נא.) גבי הנהו דמפרשו חלתא מארוזא, דאמרינן: דאי רובא לאו אורז אכלי, ניכלה זר באנפייהו, דלמא אתו לאפרושי מן הפטור על החיוב; ובפ"ק דיומא (דף י.) גבי סוכת החג בחג חייבת [בעירוב] ובמזוזה ובמעשר, דקאמר התם דמדאורייתא קאמר, דאי מדרבנן דלמא אתא לאפרושי מן הפטור על החיוב; ובדמאי, הלוקח מן עובד כוכבים, למ"ד יש קנין, חייבו חכמים, ולא חשו לכך:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 26b:20:1.english: "Perhaps he will come to separate from the exempt upon the obligated, etc." - In several places we say: "[It is valid] teruma, but he must go back and separate [teruma] again," and we do not decree [lest he come to separate from the exempt upon the obligated]. There, since the first teruma [is given] to the priest, he knows full well that the second is [only] Rabbinic. And even if he had already given the first [portion] to the priest before a sage told him to go back and separate [again], nevertheless, since the priest does not return the first to him, he knows full well that the second is Rabbinic. Here, however, he thinks that he gave [it] to the priest as payment for his assistance, and [that is why] the priest retains it. And in several places one must make distinctions in [these] matters: like that [case] in Pesachim at the beginning of [the chapter] Makom Shenahagu (Pesachim 51a) regarding those who would separate challah from rice [dough], where we say that if the majority do not eat rice, let a non-priest eat it in their presence, lest they come to separate from the exempt upon the obligated; and in the first chapter of Yoma (10a) regarding [the statement that] a festival Sukkah on the Festival is obligated [in an eruv,] in a mezuzah, and in tithe, where [the Gemara] says there that it means by Torah law, for if it were by Rabbinic law, perhaps he would come to separate from the exempt upon the obligated; and in Demai, [regarding] one who purchases from a gentile, according to the one who says [a gentile] has [the power of] acquisition [in the Land of Israel to exempt produce from tithes], the Sages obligated [him], and were not concerned about this.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 26b:8:1.hebrew: בדקה שלשים יום - כי הך פלוגתא איכא לענין טיפול אבדה (ב"מ דף כח):
Tosafot on Bekhorot 26b:8:1.english: "With regard to a small animal, thirty days" - A dispute like this exists with regard to tending to a lost item (Bava Metzia 28b).
